top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) rests on a distinct physical idea, magic-wavelength trapping that cancels the light shift and lets many neutral atoms be interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free. It was demonstrated at the 1e-18 level and reproduced and surpassed independently at several laboratories. It is now an instrument that gives results about nature (gravitational redshift over a millimetre, bounds on constants and dark-matter couplings), and it is not a proposal. The two-name allocation and the citation scope are defensible, though the attribution gap to the SYRTE, NIST and PTB groups is real. Awarding it is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile; a loose connection is that he spent a year in John Hall's lab (Boulder), and Jun Ye is Hall's former student and collaborator, and he works in atomic physics and precision spectroscopy. This is not a close collaboration.
